label: org.ent.pressagency.agence-radio
description: French wire/news agency rooted in Henri Turot's early twentieth-century radio-telegraph news activity and formally established as Agence Radio / Radio-Agence télégraphique after World War I. Despite the name, it was a press agency distributing telegrams, international news, and political information to newspapers, not primarily a radio broadcaster. It was closely linked to Havas, later came under stronger French state influence, was renamed Agence Téléradio under Vichy, and disappeared during the reorganization of French information services around Liberation.

active_period.note: Historical French news agency; precursor activity from 1904, formally Agence Radio from 1918, renamed Agence Téléradio in 1941, activities largely ceased by 1943, disappeared around 1944.

contextual_aliases.note: Use for parenthesized or formulaic newspaper source attributions such as (Radio.) or Londres ... (Radio.) when publication date and surrounding dispatch pattern support Agence Radio rather than a broadcaster.

annotation_note: In 1920s-1940s French newspaper dispatches, isolated source formulas such as (Radio.) can refer to Agence Radio, by analogy with (Havas.) or (Reuter.). Do not treat bare Radio as a generic news-agency mention outside this source-attribution pattern.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep Agence/Agentur when it is part of the proper name Agence Radio, Agence Télégraphique Radio, Radio-Agence télégraphique, or Radio-Agentur.

label: org.ent.pressagency.akp
description: Cambodia's official state news agency, established in late 1978 under the historical name Sarpordamean Kampuchea (SPK) and renamed Agence Kampuchea Presse / Agence Kampuchea Press (AKP) after the 1993 elections.

active_period.note: Known as SPK from its establishment in 1978 until its post-1993 renaming as AKP; still active.

contextual_aliases.note: Normalize SPK to AKP when Cambodian, Kampuchean, or Phnom Penh context identifies the state news agency, especially in 1978-1993 reporting. Do not confuse it with the Swiss SPK/SMP agency.

annotation_note: Use org.ent.pressagency.akp for Cambodian/Kampuchean SPK and modern AKP. In phrases such as l'agence cambodgienne SPK, the classifier resolves the acronym but stays outside the span; annotate SPK. AKP alone is ambiguous and requires Cambodia, Kampuchea, Phnom Penh, or explicit news-agency context; AKP Phnom Penh is strong positive evidence. German descriptive searches such as Nachrichtenagentur Kambodscha or kambodschanische Nachrichtenagentur are discovery queries, not standalone aliases to annotate unless the context identifies AKP/SPK. Swiss SPK references belong to org.ent.pressagency.spk-smp.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep Agence Kampuchea Presse/Press as the official AKP name; strip generic classifiers before SPK/AKP, for example agence cambodgienne SPK -> SPK.

label: org.ent.pressagency.ata
description: Albanian national news agency based in Tirana. The Albanian Telegraphic Agency is commonly abbreviated ATA in English and appears as Agjencia Telegrafike Shqiptare / ATSH in Albanian; historical German and French newspaper material may render it descriptively as Albanische Nachrichtenagentur or agence télégraphique albanaise.

active_period.note: Founded in 1920; still active as Albania's national news agency.

annotation_note: Use org.ent.pressagency.ata for ATA/ATSH and established full names such as Albanian Telegraphic Agency, Agjencia Telegrafike Shqiptare, or Agence télégraphique albanaise. In descriptive phrases such as Die albanische Nachrichtenagentur ATA bestätigte, the classifier resolves the acronym but stays outside the span; annotate ATA.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep established full official-language names such as Albanian Telegraphic Agency, Agjencia Telegrafike Shqiptare, or Agence télégraphique albanaise; strip generic classifiers before ATA/ATSH.

label: org.ent.pressagency.cip

fr: agence de presse catholique belge CIP

description: Belgian Catholic religious-news agency based in Brussels. The Centre d'information de presse (CIP) was created in 1944 by Belgian Catholic newspapers with support from church authorities. It supplied daily religious news and a weekly bulletin, worked closely with the Swiss APIC agency, split into autonomous French- and Dutch-language organizations in 1991, and ceased press-agency activity at the end of 2001.

active_period.note: Founded after the liberation of Belgium in 1944; the French-language Brussels agency ceased activity on 31 December 2001. French- and Dutch-language operations had become autonomous in 1991.

contextual_aliases.note: Use bare CIP only when an explicit press-agency or dispatch context identifies the Belgian Catholic agency, for example Wie die Agentur CIP meldet or selon l'agence CIP. Do not globally match arbitrary CIP acronyms.

annotation_note: Annotate CIP as org.ent.pressagency.cip when the context identifies the Belgian Catholic news agency. Explicit classifier forms such as Agentur CIP, Agence CIP, or agence de presse CIP are positive evidence, but annotate the core acronym CIP; keep Centre d'information de presse as the full proper-name span. Bare CIP requires agency, religious-news, Brussels/Belgian, or dispatch-source context because the acronym is ambiguous.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep Centre d’information de presse as part of the full proper name. For Agentur CIP, Agence CIP, or agence de presse CIP, strip the classifier and annotate CIP.

label: org.ent.pressagency.reuters
description: International news agency founded in London in 1851 by Paul Julius Reuter. In historical German and French newspaper text it often appears as Reuter, Reuters, or Agence Reuters; it remains an active global news provider.
annotation_note: Annotate Reuters/Reuter when it refers to the news agency, its reports, institutional activity, staff, offices, or media-source role. Do not annotate stock-market quotation tables, securities listings, or share-price reports where Reuters appears only as a traded company/security entry among other stocks.

active_period.note: Founded in 1851; still active.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Omit Agence/Agentur/agency classifiers when followed by the proper short name Reuter or Reuters. Annotate Reuter/Reuters in Agence Reuter, Agentur Reuter, or agence Reuters.

label: org.ent.pressagency.stefani
description: Italian press agency founded in 1853 by Guglielmo Stefani and active until 1945. Historical French/German material may mention it as Stefani, Agenzia Stefani, or Agence Stefani.

active_period.note: Historical Italian agency; dissolved after World War II.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Omit Agence/agency classifiers when followed by the proper short name Stefani. Annotate Stefani in Agence Stefani or agence Stefani.

label: org.ent.pressagency.extel
description: British Exchange Telegraph Company, founded in London in 1872 and later widely known as Extel. It supplied news and especially financial/market information; historical snippets may contain Exchange, Exchange Telegraph, or Extel.

active_period.note: Founded as Exchange Telegraph Company; later financial-information brand Extel.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep Exchange Telegraph Company as the full official name. Strip generic classifiers in Agence Extel/agency Extel unless the source clearly uses that exact form as a proper name.

label: org.ent.pressagency.havas
description: French news agency founded in 1835 by Charles-Louis Havas and active as Agence Havas until 1940. It is a central predecessor of Agence France-Presse; annotate historical mentions such as Havas and Agence Havas with this label.

active_period.note: Historical news-agency activity; AFP was created from the information branch in 1944.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Omit Agence/Agentur when followed by the proper short name Havas. Annotate Havas in Agence Havas, agence de presse Havas, or Agentur Havas.

label: org.ent.pressagency.xinhua
description: Chinese state news agency founded in 1931, historically also known in English as New China News Agency and in French as Chine nouvelle or Agence Chine nouvelle. It is the official press agency of the People's Republic of China.

active_period.note: Founded in 1931; still active.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep Xinhua News Agency, New China News Agency, Chine Nouvelle, and Agence Chine nouvelle as established names; strip generic classifiers before Xinhua.

label: org.ent.pressagency.domei
description: Japanese news agency created in 1935 and active until 1945 as the official news agency of the Empire of Japan. Historical labels include Domei, Dōmei Tsushin, Dōmei News Agency, and Agence de presse Dōmei.

active_period.note: Created in 1935; dissolved after World War II.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep Domei News Agency when visible as an English proper-name form; strip generic classifiers before Domei.

label: org.ent.pressagency.belga
description: Belgian news agency founded in 1920. In French historical text it often appears as Belga, Agence Belga, or Agence télégraphique belge de presse; it remains active as Belgium’s national news agency.

active_period.note: Founded in 1920; still active.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Omit Agence/agency classifiers when followed by the proper short name Belga. Annotate Belga in Agence Belga or agence Belga.

label: org.ent.pressagency.ctk
description: Czech/Czechoslovak public-service news agency originally founded in 1918 as Česká tisková kancelář. For historical material, CTK/ČTK may refer to the Czechoslovak agency, commonly rendered in German as Tschechoslowakische Nachrichtenagentur or Tschechoslowakisches Nachrichtenbüro; the modern Czech News Agency continues after 1992.

active_period.note: Founded in 1918; modern Czech agency continues after 1992.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep Czech News Agency and established full names such as Československá tisková kancelář; strip generic classifiers before CTK/ČTK/Ceteka.

label: org.ent.pressagency.palach-press
description: London-based Czechoslovak exile press and literary agency associated with Jan Kavan. Palach Press disseminated information from Czechoslovakia to Western journalists and Czechoslovak exile journalists during the communist period, especially in connection with the alternative public sphere, Charter 77, and other dissident material.

active_period.note: Czechoslovak exile press and literary agency active in London. The Charles University thesis describes Palach Press as operating in the 1970s and 1980s; the Wikidata/Czech Wikipedia metadata gives 1975-1990.

annotation_note: Annotate the proper name Palach Press / Palach Press Agency. Do not map descriptive phrases such as agence de presse tchèque dissidente or agence de presse tchécoslovaque en exil to CTK/ČTK when they describe Palach Press. If the proper name is present with a descriptive apposition, prefer only the proper-name span unless the project guidelines decide to include descriptive appositions.

metadata_sources.citation: Poláková, Tereza. Palach Press: tisková a literární agentura. Studie o exilové agentuře a komparace její prezentace událostí s oficiálními československými médii. Praha, 2020. Diplomová práce (Mgr.), Univerzita Karlova, Fakulta sociálních věd, Institut Komunikačních studií a žurnalistiky.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep Palach Press and Palach Press Agency as proper names; strip descriptive classifiers such as agence dissidente before the proper name.

label: org.ent.pressagency.ansa
description: Italian national news agency founded in 1945 as Agenzia Nazionale Stampa Associata. Historical and modern mentions usually use ANSA or the full Italian name.

active_period.note: Founded in 1945; still active.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep Agenzia Nazionale Stampa Associata as the official Italian name; strip generic classifiers in agence de presse italienne ANSA or italienische Nachrichtenagentur ANSA and annotate ANSA.

label: org.ent.pressagency.dnb
description: Deutsches Nachrichtenbüro, a German press agency controlled by the Nazi state, active from 1934 to 1945. Historical text often writes DNB, D.N.B., Deutsches Nachrichtenbüro, or Deutsches Nachrichtenburo.

active_period.note: Nazi-state controlled German agency.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep Deutsches Nachrichtenbüro and Deutsches Nachrichtenbuero as official names; strip generic classifiers before DNB.

label: org.ent.pressagency.wolff
description: Wolffs Telegraphisches Bureau, the first German news agency, founded in 1849 and active until its merger into DNB in 1933/1934. From 1865 it operated under the bank- and state-backed corporate frame of the Continental-Telegraphen-Compagnie. The public agency and dispatch-source names Wolff and W.T.B. remained common, while Continental Telegraph Company, The Continental, Agence Continentale, and related forms may denote the same Wolff/Continental agency complex.

active_period.note: Historical German agency; absorbed/replaced in the DNB era.

contextual_aliases.note: Use for parenthesized or formulaic newspaper source attributions such as Berlin, 25. Febr. (Conti.) when date and context support the Wolff/Continental agency complex. Treat this as a contextual source or service abbreviation, not as a general alias in running text.
Semi-official news service of the Wolff/Continental agency complex. Normalize explicit service-name mentions to org.ent.pressagency.wolff.

annotation_note: Normalize Continental company names and explicit Conti-Nachrichtendienst mentions to org.ent.pressagency.wolff because this inventory treats the Wolff/Continental agency complex as one canonical entity. Normalize bare Conti only in a clear dispatch-source formula such as (Conti.); leave unrelated or ambiguous running-text uses unannotated.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Omit Agence/Agentur/agency classifiers when followed by the proper short name Wolff or WTB. Keep lexicalized bureau/company names such as Wolffs Telegraphisches Bureau and Continental-Telegraphen-Compagnie.

label: org.ent.pressagency.afp
description: Agence France-Presse, international French news agency created in 1944 with institutional roots in Agence Havas. Historical snippets may show AFP, A.F.P., Agence France Presse, or Agence France-Presse.

active_period.note: Created in 1944; roots in Havas founded in 1835; still active.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep Agence France-Presse / Agence France Presse as the official name; strip generic classifiers before AFP.

label: org.ent.pressagency.up-upi
description: American international news-agency label covering historical United Press (founded 1907) and United Press International, the UPI name used after the 1958 merger of United Press with International News Service. Annotate UP, UPI, United Press, and United Press International mentions with this label when they refer to the agency.

active_period.note: United Press founded 1907; UPI name after 1958 merger; still exists in reduced form.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep United Press and United Press International as proper names; strip generic classifiers before UP/UPI.

label: org.ent.pressagency.ats-sda
description: Swiss national news agency founded in 1895, known in French as Agence télégraphique suisse (ATS) and in German as Schweizerische Depeschenagentur (SDA). The modern successor branding is Keystone-SDA.
annotation_note: Annotate ATS, SDA, Agence télégraphique suisse, Schweizerische Depeschenagentur, and explicit Keystone-SDA forms with this label. Do not annotate bare Keystone as ATS-SDA unless the visible text explicitly identifies Keystone-SDA or the context clearly names the modern Keystone-SDA agency rather than a photo credit or unrelated Keystone mention.

active_period.note: Founded in 1895; modern successor Keystone-SDA.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep Agence télégraphique suisse and Schweizerische Depeschenagentur as established official names; strip generic classifiers before ATS/SDA/Keystone-SDA.

label: org.ent.pressagency.keystone
description: Swiss press-photo agency founded in Zurich in 1953 by Max Schneider as Keystone-Press, Max Schneider. It developed into Switzerland's largest picture agency, later operating as Keystone Press AG and Keystone AG. Keystone merged with the Swiss Telegraphic Agency (SDA/ATS) effective 1 January 2018 to form the multimedia news agency Keystone-SDA/Keystone-ATS.

active_period.note: Independent Swiss Keystone photo-agency lineage from its Zurich founding in 1953 through 31 December 2017; merged with SDA/ATS effective 1 January 2018.

annotation_note: Use org.ent.pressagency.keystone for historical mentions and photo credits identifying the Swiss Keystone picture agency, including bare Keystone in a clear credit such as (Keystone), Keystone Press, or explicit photo-agency forms. Keep this entity separate from ATS/SDA before their 2018 merger. Use org.ent.pressagency.ats-sda for explicit post-merger Keystone-SDA or Keystone-ATS forms. Do not annotate unrelated uses of the ordinary word keystone or the distinct foreign Keystone Press Agency unless the context identifies the Swiss agency represented in this inventory.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep Keystone photo agency when the full proper-name phrase is visible; strip generic classifiers before Keystone.

label: org.ent.pressagency.kyodo
description: Japanese nonprofit cooperative news agency established on 1 November 1945 after the dissolution of Domei. Kyodo distributes domestic and international news to Japanese newspapers and broadcasters; Kyodo News International has provided an overseas service since 1982.

active_period.note: Established on 1 November 1945 and still active. Domei is a predecessor but remains a separate canonical entity in this inventory.

contextual_aliases.note: Resolve KNS to Kyodo News Service only in a clear dispatch continuation or source attribution near reporting verbs such as added, said, reported, ajouté, or meldete.

annotation_note: Annotate Kyodo, Kyodo News, Kyodo News Service, and equivalent language-specific agency names. Use KNS only when nearby source-attribution context resolves it to Kyodo News Service, especially after a full Kyodo mention in the same passage. Keep pre-1945 Domei mentions under org.ent.pressagency.domei.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep Kyodo News and Kyodo News Service as proper names; strip generic classifiers before Kyodo/KNS.

label: org.ent.pressagency.dpa
description: Deutsche Presse-Agentur, German press agency founded in 1949. It appears as dpa, DPA, Deutsche Presse-Agentur, Deutsche Presse Agentur, or German Press Agency.

active_period.note: Founded in 1949; still active.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep Deutsche Presse-Agentur and Deutsche Presse Agentur as official names; strip generic classifiers before DPA/dpa.

label: org.ent.pressagency.kipa
description: Swiss bilingual Catholic press agency founded in 1917, known in German as Katholische internationale Presseagentur (Kipa) and in French as Agence de presse internationale catholique (APIC). It was integrated into Swiss Catholic media centers in 2015.

active_period.note: Operated as KIPA/APIC; integrated into Catholic media centers in 2015.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep Katholische Internationale Presseagentur and Agence de presse internationale catholique as established full names; do not strip these full forms to APIC/KIPA automatically.

description: Generic source-marker bucket from the legacy thesis data, not a real news agency. Treat bare ag., agence, or Agentur as non-trainable unless a specific canonical organization can be resolved from context.

active_period.note: Not an organization; kept only to document excluded legacy material.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Do not use generic agency words as a name. This label is only for unresolved formulaic agency markers when explicitly allowed by the curation policy.

label: org.ent.pressagency.ap
description: Associated Press, nonprofit American news agency founded in 1846 and still active internationally. Historical text may use AP, A.P., Associated Press, or The Associated Press.

active_period.note: Founded in 1846; still active.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Omit generic agency classifiers before AP. Keep Associated Press as the official name.

label: org.ent.pressagency.apa
description: Austria Presse Agentur, Austria’s national news agency in its modern independent cooperative form from 1946. The longer Austrian agency lineage reaches back to nineteenth-century press bureaux, but annotate APA/Austria Presse Agentur mentions with this modern agency label.

active_period.note: Modern APA founded in 1946; older Austrian agency lineage is separate context.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Omit generic agency classifiers before APA. Keep Austria Presse Agentur, Austria-Presse-Agentur, Austria Press Agentur, and Austria Press Agency as proper-name forms.

label: org.ent.pressagency.ddp-dapd
description: German ddp/dapd label for the Deutscher Depeschendienst lineage and the later dapd Nachrichtenagentur. ddp originated in 1971 from former UPI-service staff; dapd was formed around 2010 from ddp and the German AP service and went bankrupt in 2012/2013.

active_period.note: Covers ddp lineage and later dapd; dapd operated mainly 2010-2013.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep Deutscher Depeschendienst, Deutscher Auslands-Depeschendienst, DDP, and DAPD as proper names; strip generic classifiers before DDP/DAPD.

label: org.ent.pressagency.tass
description: Soviet and Russian state news agency founded as the Telegraph Agency of the Soviet Union in 1925, later known as ITAR-TASS and Russian News Agency TASS. Historical texts may use TASS/Tass or language-specific forms of the Soviet telegraph agency name. Do not automatically collapse earlier Russian imperial or ROSTA predecessor agencies to this label unless the visible mention names TASS.

active_period.note: Founded in 1925 as the Telegraph Agency of the Soviet Union; still active as TASS. Earlier Russian imperial and ROSTA agencies are predecessor organizations, not identical training labels.

en: Telegraph Agency of the Soviet Union

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep TASS/Tass, ITAR-TASS, Russian News Agency TASS, and Telegraph Agency of the Soviet Union as proper names; strip generic classifiers before Tass/Itar-Tass.

label: org.ent.pressagency.st-petersburg-telegraph-agency
description: Russian imperial state news agency founded in 1904 as the St. Petersburg Telegraph Agency, Russia's first official news agency. In German historical newspapers it may appear descriptively as Russische Telegraphen-Agentur. It is a predecessor in the later Russian/Soviet state news-agency chain, but should be kept distinct from ROSTA and from TASS for annotation.

active_period.note: Founded in 1904 as the St. Petersburg Telegraph Agency; later Petrograd Telegraph Agency. In 1918 the Soviet-period ROSTA agency followed in the succession chain.

annotation_note: Use this label for 1904-1918 mentions of the Russian imperial/Petersburg telegraph agency, including German forms such as Russische Telegraphen-Agentur. Preserve the visible OCR surface in the span. Do not map these predecessor mentions to org.ent.pressagency.tass.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep St. Petersburg/Petrograd Telegraph Agency and historical renderings such as Russische Telegraphen-Agentur or Petersburger Telegraphen-Agentur as proper names; strip generic classifiers before short aliases such as PTA/SPTA.

label: org.ent.pressagency.europapress
description: Spanish private news agency founded in 1953. In local historical labels and OCR variants it may appear as Europapress, Europa Press, Europapresz, or abbreviated forms such as Europapr.

active_period.note: Founded in 1953; still active.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep Europapress as the proper name; strip generic classifiers before it.

label: org.ent.pressagency.spk-smp
description: Swiss political/news correspondence label covering Schweizerische Politische Korrespondenz (SPK) and Schweizer Mittelpresse (SMP). The SPK is documented from 1917 to 1993; historical snippets may contain SPK, SMP, Schweizer Mittelpresse, or the full German name.

active_period.note: Historical Swiss correspondence/news service label combining SPK and SMP evidence.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep Schweizerische Politische Korrespondenz and Schweizer Mittelpresse as proper names; strip generic classifiers before SPK/SMP.

label: org.ent.pressagency.tanjug
description: Yugoslav state news agency founded in 1943 as Telegrafska agencija nove Jugoslavije, the Telegraphic Agency of New Yugoslavia. Historical French and German newspapers may cite it in dispatch-source formulas as Tanjug, TANJUG, Tan Jug., or Tan-Jug.

active_period.note: Founded in 1943 as Yugoslavia's official news agency; the Serbian state-owned agency officially ceased in 2021, while the Tanjug brand continued under a private company.

annotation_note: Use for source attributions such as (Tan Jug.) or Belgrade dateline formulas where the context matches a news-agency dispatch. Do not treat Jugoslav place or nationality words alone as agency mentions.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep established full official names when visible; strip generic classifiers before Tanjug or Tan-Jug.

label: org.ent.pressagency.telegraphen-union
description: German news agency founded in 1913 in Berlin and later associated with Alfred Hugenberg's media group. The Telegraphen-Union was one of the main German news agencies of the Weimar period and was merged with Wolffs Telegraphisches Bureau into the Deutsches Nachrichtenbüro under National Socialist control at the end of 1933 / beginning of 1934.

active_period.note: Founded in 1913; merged into the Deutsches Nachrichtenbüro in late 1933 / early 1934.

contextual_aliases.note: Use only for parenthesized or formulaic German/Swiss newspaper source attributions such as Berlin, 7. Januar. (UTA) when the date and context fit the Weimar-period Telegraphen-Union. Treat this as a contextual source abbreviation, not as a general alias in running text.
Dotted variant of the contextual UTA source formula.

annotation_note: Use for the German news agency in Telegraphen-Union / T.U. references and contextual source formulas such as (UTA) in Weimar-period German political dispatches. Do not map UTA to ATS/SDA. Reject homonymous references to the international telegraph/radiotelegraph organization, especially administrative contexts such as Internationales Bureau der Telegraphen-Union, telecommunications departments, officials, secretaries, appointments, treaties, or member states.

agency_word_boundary_policy.note: Keep Telegraphen-Union as the proper name; strip generic or descriptive classifiers such as agence, agence télégraphique, Agence semi-officielle, or Nachrichtenagentur before the name. Do not include unrelated institutional classifiers such as Internationales Bureau der Telegraphen-Union unless the whole expression is a confirmed agency name in context.
